tagline: Colombia's 'City of Eternal Spring' turned itself from the world's most dangerous city into a model of urban innovation, strung together by cable cars over green mountains. It is ranked #35 on Time Out's Best Cities 2026 list.
overview: Medellín sits in a mountain valley at 1,500 metres, giving it its famous springlike climate. Founded in 1675, it grew rich on coffee and textiles before the drug wars of the 1980s and 90s made it infamous — the era of Pablo Escobar cast a long shadow.

The turnaround since is one of urbanism's great stories. Metrocable gondolas link once-isolated hillside barrios to the metro, and Comuna 13, formerly a no-go zone, now welcomes visitors to escalators, street art and hip-hop tours. Botero Plaza displays 23 sculptures by Medellín's most famous artist.

Paisas — locals — fill the cafés of El Poblado and Laureles, dance salsa into the night, and welcome the world at August's Feria de las Flores flower festival. Day trips climb the rock of Guatapé over a lake of drowned valleys or ride the cable car into the forests of Parque Arví.

funFacts.title: THE GREAT TURNAROUND
funFacts.text: Once called the world's most violent city, Medellín won awards as the world's most innovative city in 2013.

funFacts.title: ETERNAL SPRING
funFacts.text: At 1,500 metres on the equator, temperatures sit near 22°C all year.

funFacts.title: METROCABLES
funFacts.text: Medellín pioneered commuter cable cars, carrying millions a year over the barrios.

funFacts.title: COMUNA 13
funFacts.text: Outdoor escalators climb the hillside of a neighbourhood once ruled by gangs — now a street-art destination.

funFacts.title: BOTERO'S HOMETOWN
funFacts.text: Fernando Botero, famous for his 'fat' sculptures, donated dozens of works to the plaza and museum.

funFacts.title: THE FLOWER FESTIVAL
funFacts.text: August's Feria de las Flores fills the city with parades and farmers carrying giant flower arrangements.

funFacts.title: A ROCK TO CLIMB
funFacts.text: The Piedra del Peñol near Guatapé rewards 740 steps with a view over a maze of blue-water islands.

funFacts.title: COFFEE COUNTRY
funFacts.text: The city is the gateway to Colombia's UNESCO-listed Coffee Triangle.

funFacts.title: ONLY METRO IN COLOMBIA
funFacts.text: Medellín's metro is the country's only one — a point of intense local pride.

funFacts.title: SALSA CAPITAL
